newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr rises briefly on Sakakibara comment,then falls.
newsitem.headline: Dlr rises briefly on Sakakibara comment,then falls.

text.p: *Dollar rose briefly in mid-morning Tokyo on comment from Ministry of Finance's (MOF) Sakakibara saying it would be difficult to procure funds for foreign exchange intervention directly from the money market, then fell on comment from different MOF official that Japan can use $220 billion in external reserves promptly if needed.
*Market took Sakakibara's comment to mean it would be difficult to intervene to control dollar's rise, prompting dollar buying for yen, dealers said.

*Sakakibara, director-general of MOF's International Finance Bureau, said: "If (MOF) procures intervention funds from the money market, that would send a signal that intervention is on its way." But he added: "It's common among other nations that intervention funds are raised via central banks and the treasury account... Thus it would be extremely difficult to raise funds from the market."

*Currently, most of the funds for intervention are procured through the issuing of special foreign exchange bills, called financing bills (FBs), that have been mostly underwritten by the Bank of Japan (BOJ).
*Sakakibara's comments sparked short-covering by interbank dealers. Dollar briefly rose as high as 125.57 yen after stop-loss buying triggered near 125.30 yen, a city bank dealer said.
*But it quickly fell on the MOF official's comments that it is possible for Japan to use its external reserves in foreign exchange market prompty if needed, dealers said.
*The MOF official said Sakakibara's remarks meant there would be some problems in raising funds from the market directly without them being underwritten by the BOJ.
*Dollar edged down vs yen after key 182nd 10-year JGB yield rose 0.1 percent to 2.520 percent, while Tokyo stock market's key index opened down 34.31 points at 20,146.61.
*Stop-loss sales near 125.10 yen were triggered, pushing dollar down below 125 yen, a city bank dealer said. Another bank dealer said further stop-loss sales may emerge near 124.85 yen.
*But support expected near 124.80 yen for now. --- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-8584
